Commit `d66d79ea5f` hides OrcaSlicer's pop-up notifications inside the JusPrin shell and redraws them as a "print issues" status pill in the canvas's lower right corner, a list the pill opens, and a bubble beside the affected object with **Ask AI** and **Resolve with AI**. Reading the drawing code confirms your complaint: the list closes only if you press the pill again, and the bubble has no way to close at all. It goes away only when OrcaSlicer stops reporting the issue ([IssueOverlay.cpp:227](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/IssueOverlay.cpp:227), [IssueOverlay.cpp:325](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/IssueOverlay.cpp:325)).

I read "the bubble at the bottom right" as the issue list, which in your screenshot holds one row.

## Principle

Closing hides the view; it never resolves or ignores the issue. The pill keeps its count and is always the way back, so closing is safe and needs no confirmation.

## Proposed behaviour

**The bubble follows the object's selection.** Opening an issue already selects its object through OrcaSlicer. I propose the reverse as well: when that object stops being selected, the bubble closes. The gestures people already use to let go of an object then close it.

| Gesture | Result |
|---|---|
| Click empty plate or background | Bubble closes |
| Escape | Bubble closes (an open tool takes Escape first, as today) |
| Click another object | Bubble closes |
| Press × in the bubble's top right corner | Bubble closes, object stays selected |
| Orbit, pan, zoom, or drag the object | Bubble stays and follows |
| Press the pill | Opens or closes the list |
| Click outside the open list, or Escape | List closes |

The × is still needed: it is the only visible cue, and a plate-wide issue has no object to deselect.

**One transient surface at a time.** Picking a row closes the list, as a menu does. To step through several issues without reopening it, the bubble's pager becomes "‹ 2 of 5 ›" across all issues; today it only cycles the findings on one object.

**One issue skips the list.** In your screenshot the list row and the bubble show the same sentence twice. With exactly one issue, pressing the pill opens and closes the bubble directly.

**The pill shows its state.** It gets a pressed look and a small chevron while the list is open, so it reads as the control that closes it.

**After a button press.** **Resolve with AI** closes the bubble, because the work has moved to the chat and the object may change. **Ask AI** leaves it open so **Resolve with AI** is one click away after reading the answer.

The confirmations above the pill (for example "export finished") already have a ×; I would leave them as they are.

## Decisions for you

1. **Selection-bound bubble.** The catch is that clicking a neighbouring object to move it closes the bubble. The alternative is to close only on ×, Escape and empty-plate clicks.
2. **List closes on row pick, with the pager across all issues.** The alternative keeps the list open as an overview beside the bubble.
3. **Ask AI keeps the bubble, Resolve with AI closes it.** The alternative is that both close it.
4. **No "ignore this warning".** OrcaSlicer lets a person close a warning for good. I would keep that out for now, because the current rule is that only OrcaSlicer retires an issue.

## Not yet verified

Nothing was built or run. From reading the code, OrcaSlicer deselects on Escape and on an empty-plate click ([GLCanvas3D.cpp:3473](src/slic3r/GUI/GLCanvas3D.cpp:3473)), so the selection-bound bubble and the × should need only JusPrin's own files. I have not checked whether Escape can close the list when no object is selected without a line in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
go with your recommendations. 1 and 2 ok. 3: ask ai also closes it. 4. add a way to ignore a warning too as long as no add'l footprint on upstream

description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:

---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

name: harness-gl-readback-capture
description: "When the Mac screen is locked the shell harness's screen-blit captures come back blank (2.8 KB PNGs); read the canvas's own pixels with glReadPixels(GL_FRONT) after render() instead"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`write_screen_capture` / `blit_screen` in `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` photograph the desktop through `wxScreenDC`. With the screen locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked` prints a line) every PNG is a blank ~2.8 KB file and no check fails.

For anything drawn inside the GL canvas (ImGui overlays, the tool strip, bubbles) read the frame back instead: `prepare_canvas().render()`, then `glReadBuffer(GL_FRONT)` and `glReadPixels` over `get_canvas_size()`, flip vertically into a `wxImage`, save as PNG. Worked on 2026-10-08 with the screen locked and the window inactive; needs `#include <glad/gl.h>`. Native notifications drawn by Orca are in the same frame, so they appear too. Web views still need `capture_web_view`.

Side effect of an inactive window: Orca's `NotificationManager::update_notifications` returns early, so closed popups are never retired and `get_notification_count()` only grows.

Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[screenshots-to-files-via-page-fixture]].

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

The print-issue list and bubble on the Prepare canvas can now be closed in the ways we agreed, and a warning can be ignored. No OrcaSlicer-owned file changed. The work is uncommitted in a new worktree, `.claude/worktrees/print-issue-dismissal` (branch `claude/print-issue-dismissal`, based on `d66d79ea5f`).

## What it does now

- **Bubble closes with the selection.** A click on the empty plate, Escape, or a click on another object closes it. Turning the view or dragging the object keeps it open.
- **Close button.** The × in the bubble's top right closes it and leaves the object selected. For a plate-wide issue, which has no object, the × and Escape are the ways out.
- **Ask AI and Resolve with AI** both close the bubble once the message reaches the chat. If no assistant is set up, the bubble stays.
- **List.** It closes on picking a row, a second press of the pill, Escape, or a press anywhere outside it. Opening the list closes the bubble, so only one is open at a time.
- **Pager.** With several issues the bubble shows "‹ 2 of 5 ›" and walks all of them.
- **One issue skips the list.** The pill opens and closes the bubble directly.
- **Pill state.** It shows a chevron when it opens a list and looks pressed while something is open.
- **Ignore this warning.** A link under the two buttons; the bubble closes and the pill stops counting that warning. It stays in the list below the others, marked "Ignored", and its bubble offers "Stop ignoring".

## Choices I made on ignoring

- **It is a JusPrin-side mark, not a close of OrcaSlicer's notification.** Closing the notification would bring the warning back at the next edit and would also close every other warning of the same kind.
- **Correction:** I said earlier that OrcaSlicer lets a person close a warning "for good". That was wrong; it returns at the next edit.
- **Blockers cannot be ignored**, because OrcaSlicer would still refuse to print.
- **The pill never says "No print issues" over an ignored warning.** It says "1 warning ignored".
- **An ignore lasts while OrcaSlicer keeps reporting that warning.** It survives edits, a slice and a plate switch. If the warning goes away and later comes back, it is shown again.
- **It is not saved with the project.** Say so if you want either of the last two changed.

## What it does

- **Hidden when clear.** The chip is drawn only while OrcaSlicer reports at least one issue.
- **Still shown for ignored warnings.** With only ignored warnings left it reads "1 warning ignored", because it is the way back to un-ignore them.
- **Does not vanish early.** After an edit, the chip stays and reads "Checking..." until OrcaSlicer has re-checked, so its disappearance always means a real all-clear.
- **Animation on arrival.** When an issue appears that was not in the list before, a ring in the colour of the chip's dot (amber for a warning, red for a blocker) spreads outward from the chip and fades, twice, over 1.4 seconds. It then stops and does not loop.
- **What does not trigger it.** An edit that keeps the same issue, ignoring a warning, and undoing an ignore are all silent. An issue that clears and later returns is announced again.
- **Confirmations move down.** Messages such as "export finished" now sit in the corner itself when the chip is hidden.

Inside the JusPrin shell OrcaSlicer's own pop-up notifications are held but
no longer drawn. JusPrin reads the list back and draws what it holds:

- Print problems: a status in the lower right corner of the Prepare canvas,
  the list it opens, and a bubble beside the object the selected issue is
  about, with Ask AI and Resolve with AI.
- The outcome of an action (export finished, an arrange that was refused): a
  short confirmation above the status, with a close button that closes
  OrcaSlicer's own notification.
- Work that is still running (a slice, an arrange, an export): an entry in
  the chat with a progress bar and, where the work can be stopped, Cancel.

This is two commits from feature-popup-message-handling as one: the first
print-issues design (6394191523), which was taken off this branch for a
rethink, and the redesign that followed (0c3bbcce42).

OrcaSlicer's notification list is the source of truth. PrintIssues/NoticeKinds
routes each of its 62 notification kinds: print problem, outcome of an
...

PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor is told to look again on the first line of
NotificationManager::update_notifications, compares cheaply, and rebuilds
only on a change. While OrcaSlicer holds an edit it has not yet applied to
the print, the issues are marked stale, the status says it is checking, and
the buttons are off, so "no print issues" is never shown before a check.
Only the active plate is reported, because that is the only plate OrcaSlicer
checks. "Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's own answer, never a stricter test
of the fork's.

Canvas (PrintIssues/IssueOverlay, IssueOverlayLayout): drawn with ImGui
through the overlay hook the tool strip uses. The bubble goes above its
object, else right, left or below, and never covers the object, the status,
the open list, a confirmation or the tool strip. It docks beside the status
for a plate-wide issue or an object out of view. Every finding on one object
shares the bubble through a pager. Selecting an issue selects its copy by
OrcaSlicer's own id.

Ask AI or Resolve with AI becomes an ordinary user message, the request
sentence with OrcaSlicer's words quoted beneath it, and carries the issue,
